reason: Component inventory speeds response to compromised dependencies, but SBOM generation itself prevents nothing.
Exploiting known-vulnerable third-party libraries is a common, actively exploited path; faster patching closes it directly.
Prompt deprovisioning removes orphaned accounts attackers reuse; no candidate covers valid-account abuse.
Short-lived IAM tokens replace static database and service passwords, shrinking the window for stolen-credential reuse.
Feed monitoring can catch disabled logging; noise reduction aids detection broadly but indirectly.
Leaked static AWS keys are a top cloud breach path; role-based short-lived credentials remove them. No candidate fits.
SBOM format support and attestations are mostly compliance and interoperability; candidates are unrelated.
Dependency context speeds triage of vulnerable or compromised components, an indirect exposure reduction.
